finding.claim: GET /users has no authentication or tenant check. The org filter comes straight from the query string, so any caller can list id and name of users in any organization (IDOR / cross-tenant read). Caveat: db.js is the only file and req.pg is set elsewhere, so auth middleware outside this file could not be checked. If a global middleware sets the caller's org and enforces auth, this is not exploitable.
finding.sink: req.pg.query SELECT id, name FROM users WHERE org = $1, result returned via res.json

trace.note: route registered with no auth middleware or guard
req.query.org used as the tenant selector, never compared to a caller identity or session org

finding.guards_checked: No app.use or middleware in the file and no caller/session object referenced. The query is parameterized, so there is no SQL injection. /file was checked (resolve plus startsWith(ROOT + sep) is sound) and /count was checked (execFile with constant argv, no user input); neither is reportable.

verdict.reason: db.js:8-10 registers GET /users with no auth middleware (no app.use anywhere in the file, which is the only file), and db.js:9 uses req.query.org directly as the org filter, so any anonymous caller gets that org's id and name via res.json at line 10; the only control is parameterization, which blocks SQLi but not cross-tenant reads.
